Version 1.2.1 introduces advanced metadata extraction, templating, and batch enhancements:

- Added YAML frontmatter support for structured metadata (title, author, date, etc.) from meta and JSON-LD tags.
- New template system allows customizable Markdown output using variables (e.g. title, content, author).
- Batch conversion improvements: smart filename templates and option to download images locally.
- Expanded command-line options for frontmatter, templating, and asset handling.
- Updated documentation and examples reflecting new features for knowledge-base workflows.
- Added LICENSE file to clarify usage and distribution terms.

- Improved extraction scope: now prioritizes content in <article> or <main>, making Markdown output focus on primary article/main content instead of the whole page.
- Enhanced title handling: prefers Open Graph and Twitter titles for better accuracy when adding H1.
- Added --full-page option to allow processing the entire <body> instead of just main/article content.
- Improved formatting: supports fenced code blocks with optional language hints, GitHub-style tables, and better bold/italic conversion.
- More comprehensive noise removal: skips forms and extra "chrome" inside extracted sections for cleaner output.

- Initial release of url2md: convert any web page to clean, readable Markdown.
- Supports single URLs and batch processing from URL lists.
- Outputs can be directed to file or directory; title extraction as H1 included by default.
- Handles standard Markdown formatting (headings, lists, links, images, code blocks, tables).
- Strips boilerplate content including scripts, styles, navigation, and footers.
- Requires no third-party dependencies; uses only Python standard library.
